outcome: Total oral morphine equivalents (mg) at 24 and 48 h
Proportion of opioid-free patients at 24 and 48 h
Frequency of ITM-related side-effects (pruritus, nausea, vomiting)
cohort: The study included 574 ASA 2 females, over 18 years old, undergoing repeat elective caesarean sections.
finding: All doses of intrathecal morphine provided effective analgesia, with 100 mcg dosing offering the best trade-off between analgesic efficacy and side effect profile, though 150 mcg provided greater analgesia and duration.
mod_finding: The study found that for patients undergoing caesarean section, a 100 mcg intrathecal morphine dose provided the best balance of analgesic efficacy and side effects compared to 125 mcg and 150 mcg doses.
